newsitem.title: INDIA: India delays implementing pay panel recommendation.
newsitem.headline: India delays implementing pay panel recommendation.

text.p: The Indian government on Monday decided to withhold implementing the recommendations of a pay panel for its 5.2 million employees, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said.
The news agency said the decision, which involved a package of 135 billion rupees, was taken following agitation from various employee unions.

"We have withheld implementations of the commission's report because we find the government has done well. We have gone way beyond the recommendations which we feel are quite generous," PTI quoted Cabinet Secretary T.S.R. Subramaniam as saying.
The Fifth Pay Commission, which submitted its report to the Finance Ministry earlier in January, recommended sizeable increases in pay packets for the government employees.
"And after paying 135 billion rupees, we find everybody is dissatisfied," Subramaniam was quoted as saying.
The employee unions said they wanted certain modifications before the recommendations of the pay panel were implemented.

PTI quoted V.S. Yadav, secretary general of the Government Employee National Confederation, as saying the junior employees were very dissatisfied with the report as its implementation would widen the gap between the lowest and the highest salaried persons.

The commission in its report had also called for the abolition of 350,000 vacant posts, constituting nearly a tenth of the current total strength of the federal government. Currently there are 3.7 million federal government workers.

Yadav said the abolition of vacant posts would badly hit the labour class. He said they are also demanding the implementation of recommendations, after modifications, from January 1, 1994 and wanted the government to pay the arrears. ($1 = 35.7 rupees).
